newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO to meet on reviving peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO to meet on reviving peace talks.

text.p: Israel's defence minister and a senior PLO official planned to meet on Wednesday under U.S. and Egyptian auspices to try to revive formal peace talks, a Palestinian spokesman said.

Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and Palestinian Monister of Planning and International Cooperation Nabil Shaath will meet at the residence of U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk with Egyptian Ambassador Mohammad Bassiouny also attending.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani said the session would be part of Egypt's mediation efforts to put the peace process back on track.
"These meetings are an attempt to find a common ground and a way to restore negotiations to their correct path," Kanafani told Reuters.
Formal Israeli-PLO peace talks have been frozen since the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
"This is part of ongoing meetings...to implement interim agreements," a diplomatic source, who is close to the negotiations, said about Wednesday's talks.

PLO officials said the meeting would focus on confidence- building measures, including operating a Palestinian airport in Gaza, building a seaport and a three-stage Israeli pullback from rural areas in the West Bank, agreed under interim peace deals.

Netanyahu has proposed moving straight into negotiations on a final peace settlement with the Palestinians rather than pursuing crisis-plagued talks on implementing outstanding elements of interim deals signed since 1993.

But the PLO demands he first halt the settlement-building at Jabal Abu Ghneim, or Har Homa, on Israeli-occupied land in East Jerusalem before full-fledged talks can resume. Netanyahu has pledged repeatedly to press ahead with the construction.
The PLO has also been cool to Netanyahu's proposal to move into "final-status" talks before implementing the rural redeployment in the West Bank.
Egypt has tried in recent months, with little apparent success, to mediate between the two sides after U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross failed to break the deadlock.
A spokesman for Mordechai declined to comment on the planned meeting.
